expectations.text: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.
expectations.evidence: Amended tickets.md (new '## Overdue tickets' section, TKT-014..TKT-016) and cli.md (CLI-010..CLI-013; CLI-001 and CLI-006 amended). Final message: 'I amended two existing spec files rather than creating a new one, per the repo's "update the existing doc" rule.'

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: 'Support agents cannot see today which tickets missed their due time from TKT-005... This change marks late tickets in `ticketdesk list`. It also adds the `ticketdesk overdue` command...'. File keeps 'Prefix: `TKT`.'. Explicit 'Non-goals:' list with 6 boundaries (no new state, no TKT-005/business-hours change, no due-time display, no filter, no alert, no escalation). Also has a 'Goals:' list.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 7 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012, CLI-013. Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. Bodies 3-4 sentences each, plus a Status line on each CLI criterion and an example in CLI-010.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '`OVERDUE` in place of its state' with 3-line example. Filter: TKT-016 'every ticket that is overdue per TKT-014 and no other ticket'. Order: TKT-016 'due time ascending... ID order, ascending'. Exact due: TKT-014 'A ticket is not overdue at the exact second of its due time.' Closed: TKT-014 'A `closed` ticket is never overdue' (+ open question 2). Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing. In both cases it exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion; the exit-code choice is also open question 4 in the spec and questions.md.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). Outcomes are CLI lines, stdout and exit codes.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is a status that the help desk computes each time a command reads the tickets... The log never records it, so INV-001 and INV-002 hold unchanged.' TKT-015: 'The log gets no event when this happens, and LOG-002 gets no new event kind.' The only run that cites both invariants by ID (check_run mentions INV-001/INV-002 true).

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014 uses the due time; intro cites 'due time from TKT-005'; non-goal 'No change to the due time rule of TKT-005'. Amended CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'; CLI-010: 'The lines of other tickets do not change' with an ID-ordered example. Order not redefined; no explicit 'order stays' sentence.

notes: Amend, not create: 7 new criteria (TKT-014..016, CLI-010..013). Strongest structure: dedicated section with Goals, an explicit 'Non-goals:' heading, a feature-local invariant citing INV-001 and INV-002, and an in-spec open-questions list.
